text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Thursday denied a media report that its headquarters had been raided by Tokyo prosecutors.
"There has been no raid at our headquarters today," said a Nomura Securities spokesman. "There was no such investigation."
Jiji news agency reported earlier on Thursday that Tokyo prosecutors had raided Nomura's headquarters.
Also earlier in the day, prosecutors charged former Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki with making illegal payoffs to corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike.

They also served Sakamaki and two other former Nomura executives with new arrest warrants alleging they conspired to pay Koike 320 million yen in cash around March 24, 1995, in exchange for a pledge by him to ensure that the firm's June shareholders' meeting went smoothly.
